assumptions.assumption: the table is not cleared by CPU_RESETN.
assumptions.reason: only the clear command zeroes the counts; the bench always clears first.

behaviour: For each presented point (x, y) and each direction index k in 0..15: rho = ((x*CT[k] + y*ST[k] + 64) >>> 7) + 48 with CT[k] = round(128 cos(k*pi/16)) and ST[k] = round(128 sin(k*pi/16)) (arithmetic shift, round-half-up); if 0 <= rho < 96 the count of (k, rho) increases by one.
A point written while BUSY is ignored; BUSY is high for about 17 clocks per point (the reference). The shell is slower than a point, so the bench never overlaps points.
LED[0] = BUSY, the other LEDs are 0.

"""Acceptance tests of c13_hough_lines against model.py (hidden from the agent)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import cocotb
from benchmark.lib.bench import Board, peek
from model import CLEAR, DESIGN_ID, PT, RD_CNT, RD_SEL, STATUS, accumulate, bench_pictures, read_bins


async def picture(b: Board, name: str, pts) -> None:
    await b.write(CLEAR, 1)
    for x, y in pts:
        await b.write(PT, x | y << 8)
    await b.expect(STATUS, 0, f"{name}: not busy after the last point")
    acc = accumulate(pts)
    for k, r in read_bins(acc):
        await b.write(RD_SEL, k | r << 8)
        await b.expect(RD_CNT, int(acc[k][r]), f"{name}: count of direction {k}, distance index {r}")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_identity_and_reset(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    assert await b.shell_id() == DESIGN_ID
    for off in (RD_SEL, STATUS):
        await b.expect(off, 0, f"reset value of {off}")


@cocotb.test()
async def test_diagonal_line(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    n, p = bench_pictures()[0]
    await picture(b, n, p)


@cocotb.test()
async def test_vertical_line(dut):
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    n, p = bench_pictures()[1]
    await picture(b, n, p)


@cocotb.test()
async def test_four_lines_then_clear(dut):
    """Several lines at once, then CLEAR and a different picture: nothing is left over."""
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    n, p = bench_pictures()[2]
    await picture(b, n, p)
    n2, p2 = bench_pictures()[0]
    await picture(b, n2 + " after clear", p2)


@cocotb.test()
async def test_corners_and_registers(dut):
    """Points at the picture corners reach the table edges (rho = -48 and +47 are inside), RD_SEL is a plain register."""
    b = Board(dut, {})
    await b.start()
    pts = [(0, 0), (31, 31), (31, 0), (0, 31), (16, 16)]
    await b.write(CLEAR, 1)
    for x, y in pts:
        await b.write(PT, x | y << 8)
    acc = accumulate(pts)
    for k in range(16):
        for r in (0, 1, 47, 48, 94, 95):
            await b.write(RD_SEL, k | r << 8)
            await b.expect(RD_CNT, int(acc[k][r]), f"corners: direction {k}, distance index {r}")
    await b.write(RD_SEL, 0xFFFF_FFFF)
    await b.expect(RD_SEL, 0x7F0F, "RD_SEL keeps k and r")
    led = await peek(b.clk, dut.LED)
    assert led == 0, f"LED {led:04X}: idle"
    for off in (0x05, 0x41, 0x7F):
        await b.expect(off, 0, "unmapped")

spec_md:
# Hough line accumulator behind the test shell

I want a block that is told where the edge points of a small picture are and then tells me which straight lines they form, and I want to exercise it entirely from the test shell.

- The picture is 32 by 32. I give the block the edge points one at a time over the shell: x and y (0 to 31) in one write, which presents the point to the block for one clock; the block takes a new point only when it is not busy,
  and it says so in a status register.
- The block looks for lines at 16 directions spaced evenly over 180 degrees (0, 11.25, 22.5 ... degrees, the angle of the line's normal) and records, for each direction, how many points would lie on
  each possible distance from the origin (whole numbers, from -48 to +47). I want to be able to read any of these counts back: I select a direction and a distance and then read the count.
- A "clear" command starts a new picture by zeroing all counts.
- I will test it with pictures of single straight lines at known angles, and with several lines at once. CPU_RESETN returns the block to idle. LED0 shows that the block is busy.
  The shell runs at 115200 baud on the USB-UART. The design ID is "HOUG".

Test hooks: top module `c13_hough_lines_top`, ports named as in the board's master XDC, and the test shell's
`CLKS_PER_BIT`, `TIMEOUT_CYCLES` and `BUILD_STAMP` parameters as top-level parameters. There are no other time
constants.

trace.stimulus: The picture of 4 straight lines on a 32 by 32 grid, which has 107 edge points. Each point votes in all 16 directions.

what: A line detector for a small edge picture. Each edge point votes for every straight line that could pass through it, in a set of evenly spaced directions, and the votes are counted in a table of direction against distance from the origin. Where many points lie on one line their votes pile up in one cell. The table can be cleared and read back cell by cell.
where: The Hough transform finds lane markings, edges of objects and straight features in machine vision, robotics and document scanning. Hardware versions run it on video streams in real time.
